ai.definition: Consciousness theories and artificial consciousness involve the study of the nature of human consciousness and its replication in machines. This technology aims to understand how conscious experiences arise from neural activity and then apply this understanding to develop AI systems that exhibit similar qualities.
ai.howItWorks: Research into consciousness theories involves analyzing brain functions, neural networks, and cognitive processes using methods from neuroscience, psychology, and philosophy of mind. Artificial consciousness attempts to model these processes in computational systems, often through the development of advanced AI algorithms and architectures designed to simulate conscious experiences.
ai.problemSolved: This technology seeks to address ethical concerns related to AI by creating more human-like and ethically aligned artificial intelligence. It also aims to improve brain-computer interface technologies that could enhance human cognitive abilities or assist individuals with disabilities.
ai.manufacturing: Manufacturing processes are not directly applicable, as this is primarily a research-driven field focusing on theoretical models and simulations rather than physical products.
ai.buildProcess: The build process involves extensive computational modeling, simulation of neural networks, and iterative testing to refine AI algorithms that mimic conscious experiences. This includes creating large-scale neural network architectures and training them with complex datasets.
ai.costDrivers: Cost drivers include the need for advanced computing resources, specialized research facilities, and interdisciplinary expertise in neuroscience, psychology, and computer science. Long-term funding is also a significant factor due to the complexity of the research.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook remains speculative but shows potential for significant advancements as more data becomes available and computational capabilities improve.
ai.regulation: Current regulatory frameworks are limited, with most efforts focused on ethical guidelines rather than specific legal standards. As the field progresses, there may be increased calls for regulation to address safety and privacy concerns.
ai.risks: Risks include potential misuse of AI technologies, ethical dilemmas related to artificial consciousness, and the possibility that current theories about consciousness are insufficient or incorrect.
ai.profitability: Profitability is uncertain due to the speculative nature of the field. While there may be long-term benefits for industries interested in advanced AI and brain-computer interfaces, immediate financial returns are unlikely.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development will likely involve closer integration between neuroscience and AI research, as well as advancements in computational methods that can better simulate complex cognitive processes.

glossary.def: Theoretical frameworks explaining the nature of consciousness and its emergence from brain activity.
An attempt to replicate conscious experiences in artificial systems, often through advanced AI techniques.

subsystems.name: Theory of consciousness
subsystems.role: supplies a testable definition of what would count as a conscious system, so engineers know what they are aiming at.

subsystems.name: Computational substrate
subsystems.role: the hardware that would run it — digital accelerators or brain-inspired chips.

subsystems.name: Architecture
subsystems.role: the software design meant to reproduce the proposed ingredients of consciousness.

subsystems.name: Embodiment and sensors
subsystems.role: gives the system a body, a viewpoint and consequences, which most theories treat as important.

subsystems.name: Measurement and testing
subsystems.role: attempts to detect consciousness rather than just intelligent behaviour.
parts: neural-correlate comparison with humans and animals

subsystems.name: Ethics and governance
subsystems.role: decides what may be done to a system that might be a moral subject.

buildSteps.title: Pick a theory with testable predictions
buildSteps.detail: Work only from accounts that say what physical arrangement should produce experience and what would falsify the claim.

buildSteps.title: Build the substrate
buildSteps.detail: Assemble compute with the recurrent, high-bandwidth connectivity the theory requires, rather than the feed-forward pattern of most current networks.

buildSteps.title: Implement the proposed mechanism
buildSteps.detail: Engineer the specific ingredient — a global workspace that broadcasts information, integrated causal structure, or a self-model tracking the system's own attention.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop with a body
buildSteps.detail: Give the system sensors and actuators so its internal states are about things in the world and its actions change what it senses.

buildSteps.title: Add metacognition
buildSteps.detail: Let it monitor and report on its own internal states, which is how humans report experience.

buildSteps.title: Test with perturbation, not chat
buildSteps.detail: Rather than judging by conversation, measure how a stimulus ripples through the system and compare with the signatures found in awake humans and animals.

buildSteps.title: Attack the result
buildSteps.detail: Try to explain every measured signature as mere information processing or clever imitation before concluding anything.

buildSteps.title: Govern it
buildSteps.detail: If evidence accumulates, apply agreed welfare and containment rules before scaling or deploying.

prerequisites.why: several serious theories exist and compete, and none is settled — so the design target is still undefined.

prerequisites.tech: Measures of consciousness in biological systems
prerequisites.why: tools such as perturbational complexity distinguish awake from unconscious human brains, but do not yet detect a machine.
neuromorphic and accelerator chips exist in labs and products, but none is designed for the specific architecture any theory demands.
projects such as the Human Brain Project produced simulation platforms, not a working mind.
embodiment is built technology; what is missing is the architecture inside it.
there is no agreed rule for treating a possibly conscious machine.

pathway.milestone: competing theories tested against brain data
pathway.unlocks: narrowing the design space for any artificial version.

pathway.milestone: theory-derived architectures benchmarked on the same indicators used for humans
pathway.unlocks: meaningful comparisons instead of claims based on fluent conversation.

pathway.milestone: an agreed, falsifiable test for machine consciousness
pathway.unlocks: research that can actually fail, and clearer ethics.

pathway.milestone: a system meeting that test, with human-equivalent or different internal structure
pathway.unlocks: moral and regulatory questions that are currently hypothetical.
